title: Pretending and Deadpan Distance with Como si

sections.content:
You know *como si* + imperfect subjunctive from B2 Unit 15 (*Habla como si lo supiera todo*, *Actuaba como si fuera el jefe*). At C1, *como si* expands to the **pluperfect subjunctive** for unreal past comparisons and pairs with pretending verbs to create deadpan humour.

Use **como si + imperfect subjunctive** (*-ra* / *-se*) when the unreal comparison is simultaneous with the main verb (*Finge una sonrisa como si el chiste fuera gracioso*). Use **como si + pluperfect subjunctive** (*hubiera / hubiese* + participle) when the imagined event lies earlier than the main verb (*Entró a la sala como si no hubiera pasado nada*; *Nos dio consejos como si hubiera dirigido diez empresas*).

In conversation, speakers also shorten the clause to the fixed chunk **como si nada** ("as if nothing had happened / casually") and pair it with *fingir* ("to pretend") or *hacerse el tonto / la tonta* ("to play dumb").

sections.title: Como si: simultaneous vs earlier unreal comparison
rows: *Se hace el tonto como si no entendiera la broma.*
*Sonrió como si hubiera dicho algo muy gracioso.*
*Llegó una hora tarde y se sentó como si nada.*
*como si ha pasado* ✗ / *como si haya pasado* ✗ → *como si hubiera pasado* ✓

items.spanish: Se echó a reír como si hubiera contado el mejor chiste del año.
items.english: He burst out laughing as if he had told the best joke of the year.

items.spanish: Cuando le preguntaron por el error, se hizo el tonto como si no supiera de qué hablaban.
items.english: When they asked him about the mistake, he played dumb as if he did not know what they were talking about.

items.spanish: Fingió una sonrisa amable y siguió hablando en serio como si nada.
items.english: She feigned a polite smile and kept talking seriously as if nothing had happened.

items.spanish: Me mira con risa contenida, como si estuviera a punto de soltar otra broma.
items.english: He looks at me with suppressed laughter, as if he were about to drop another joke.

sections.content: English "as if he has done" tempts learners into *como si haya hecho* (present perfect subjunctive), which is wrong in standard Spanish. Always use *hubiera* or *hubiese* after *como si* for an earlier unreal action.
